clue.text: Revolutionary leader introduces doctor to dance

indicators.note: the leader introduces the doctor into his own name, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Mao Zedong led the Chinese communist revolution
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A revolutionary leader brings his physician onto the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The mambo is a Cuban ballroom dance, so it is one example of a dance.

clue.text: Official is second to support party led by PM

indicators.note: being led by means coming after, so the party follows the PM
in a down answer, supporting means sitting below, so this piece goes last

parts.note: John Major was British Prime Minister 1990-97
a do is a party
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: An official is second to support a party led by the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: John Major was a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A major-domo is the chief steward of a great household, an official in charge of its servants.

clue.text: Signal translator exposed casual worker tracking Government department

indicators.note: tracking means following, so this piece comes after

parts.note: MoD is the Ministry of Defence

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer covering, so the outside letters go

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker

explanation.surface: A translator is revealed as a casual worker who follows a ministry around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' here means stripped of its outer letters, not revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem converts digital data into a signal for a phone line and back again, so it translates signals.

clue.text: Finished composition before time? No!

parts.note: over means finished

indicators.note: no here means without, so the time's letter is dropped

parts.note: a duet is a musical composition for two

explanation.surface: Was the piece done ahead of schedule? Certainly not!
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes T from DUET. 'before' links the parts but also gives the whole-clue reading: not early, but late.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means late, past its expected time, the opposite of finished before time.

clue.text: Copycat musical makes a comeback after author's appeal

indicators.note: the musical's piece comes after the author's and the appeal's letters

parts.note: the author speaking of himself says I, and 'author's' = author is = I'M
IT is sex appeal, as in the old phrase for allure

indicators.note: coming back means the musical's name is written backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A copycat musical staged again, trading on the writer's charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters call themselves 'the author', so 'author's' is I'M; 'appeal' is IT as in old slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A copycat imitates others, so a copycat product or work is imitative; here the adjective use.

clue.text: Headline-cropping Ed. up to snuff

indicators.note: up means stirred up or disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the headline crops, or cuts out, the editor's letters

parts.note: Ed. is the abbreviation for editor, and also gives its own letters ED

explanation.surface: An editor cuts a headline to meet the standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cropping' takes E and D from HEADLINE, leaving HALINE; 'up' rearranges it. 'up to snuff' is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuff is to sniff or draw in through the nose, which is to inhale.

clue.text: Spoilt devil having top quality wine

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as I
red is wine

explanation.surface: A spoilt little devil with the finest wine.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means top quality, and the digit 1 reads as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoilt has been damaged or weakened, which is what impaired means.

clue.text: Performer in Dire Straits trimmed programme's finale

indicators.note: dire means in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disarray
trimmed means a bit cut from the end, so the last letter goes
the finale is the end, so only the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A musician in the band Dire Straits trimmed the show's finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed' cuts STRAITS to STRAIT; 'Dire' rearranges that as ARTIST, then the E that ends 'programme's'. Dire Straits was a British rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer, especially a singer or dancer: a performer.

clue.text: Berlin not right to be upset about car that's too quiet

indicators.note: about means around, so the anagram goes round the car
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the remaining letters are shuffled
R is right, and it is removed

parts.note: an Audi is a German car

explanation.surface: Berlin, upset with a car that is too quiet, without a right of complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Berlin' tempts as the city or Irving Berlin; it is only fodder, minus its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaudible means unable to be heard, as a sound too quiet would be.

clue.text: Longing to do good in role of saint in festival

indicators.note: playing in the role of means standing in for, so one piece replaces another inside the festival

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

explanation.surface: Keen to play a saint, for good, at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: G takes the place of ST in EASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen, full of longing to do something, and 'Longing' here is the adjective.

clue.text: Book cool position in court

parts.note: Judges is a book of the Old Testament
hip means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: Reserve a trendy role in the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb (reserve); it is the Bible book.
explanation.definitionFit: A judgeship is the office held by a judge, a post in a law court.

clue.text: Pluck exhibited by women in Dynasty

indicators.note: the women's letter sits inside the dynasty's name

parts.note: the Tang dynasty ruled China from 618 to 907

explanation.surface: Courage shown by the women of a TV soap dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' reads as courage, but it is the verb for plucking a string; 'Dynasty' suggests the TV soap but is the Tang.
explanation.definitionFit: To twang a string is to pluck it so it makes a ringing sound.

clue.text: Change more ornate key

indicators.note: something ornate is elaborately worked, so the letters of 'more' are dressed up into a new order

parts.note: DEL is the delete key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Change a key to make it fancier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ornate' reworks MORE as REMO.
explanation.definitionFit: To remodel something is to reshape or alter it, a synonym of change as a verb.

clue.text: One of us picked up drink from pub

indicators.note: something picked up is heard, so the phrase is spoken and the spelling taken from its sound

parts.note: cider from an inn, an inn cider

explanation.surface: A regular orders a drink at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' says INN CIDER is heard, giving a word with the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is a member of the group, someone who belongs, as opposed to an outsider.

clue.text: Lots of dogs heading off

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the dog breed goes off

parts.note: poodles are dogs

explanation.surface: Plenty of dogs set off on their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes P from POODLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, so it means lots.

clue.text: For Germans, the earth is charged by the Spanish for fuel

parts.note: die is a German word for the

indicators.note: charged means loaded, filled, so the earth is loaded with the Spanish article

parts.note: soil is earth
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: German soil, energised by Spain, becomes fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' means loaded, not electrified: the earth is filled with the Spanish article.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel oil is heavy petroleum used in diesel engines, a fuel.

clue.text: Weeks of decline in retirement not entirely retaining honour

indicators.note: the reversed letters hold the honour within them
retiring means going back, so the shortened word is read backwards
not all of the word is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to recede is to decline or ebb
the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A pensioner's weeks of fading health, with a decoration kept to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE is a British honour. The definition is just 'Weeks': the month spans four and more.
explanation.definitionFit: December is a month, a span of some four and a half weeks, so 'Weeks' stands for it.

clue.text: Trial run without judges is bona fide

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the genuine word wraps the other

parts.note: bona fide means genuine, real
a judge hears a case

explanation.surface: A trial run with no judges present is genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice performance before the real event, a trial run.

clue.text: I provide evidence of depression obscuring recollection of denial

indicators.note: obscuring means covering, so the depression wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a dent is a depression in a surface

indicators.note: re-collection taken as a collection gathered back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nope is a casual denial

explanation.surface: Depression hides one's memory of having said no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollection' is read as re-collection, a gathering back, hence the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A deponent is a person who gives sworn evidence; the definition is in the first person, as the answer says 'I'.

clue.text: Unlike a coin to be biased

definitions.meaning: a coin has two sides, so something unlike it has only one

explanation.surface: Being partial, unlike a fair coin toss.
explanation.definitionFit: A biased account presents only one side; and a coin, having heads and tails, is the opposite of single-faced.

clue.text: Reserve last of tickets (by whatever means) for Frozen?

parts.note: ice means cold reserve, aloofness

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: how asks by what means

explanation.surface: Save the final tickets, any way you can, for the film Frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: Frozen is the Disney film, also staged as a skating show.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice show is a performance on skates; Disney's Frozen has toured as one, with the question mark marking the example.

clue.text: Address of No 1 boarding school

indicators.note: boarding means getting on board, so one piece gets inside the other

parts.note: 'number one' is a nursery euphemism for a pee

explanation.surface: The address of the top boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 1' is nursery slang for urinating; 'boarding' means getting inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk to an audience, which is a speech.

clue.text: Studs used to make connections by spiking drinks

indicators.note: spiking means lacing a drink with something put into it

parts.note: pop is fizzy drink, plural pops
per means by, as in per cent

explanation.surface: Studs who make connections by spiking drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Studs' suggests men on the pull, and 'poppers' a drug, but it means press studs.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppers are press studs, fasteners that snap together to join two pieces of fabric.

clue.text: Segment of burrowing earthworm's working effectively

indicators.note: Segment of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece of a burrowing earthworm is doing its job well.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine in gear is engaged and running properly, so figuratively functioning well.

clue.text: Not the same cycling around outskirts of Everest towards a specified place

indicators.note: the cycled word goes around the edge letters of the mountain
cycling moves a letter from one end of the word round to the other

parts.note: other means different, not the same

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: A different cyclist circles the fringes of Everest on the way to a named spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the first letter of the synonym round to its end before the mountain's edges go in.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereto is a formal adverb meaning to that place or thing, one already specified.

clue.text: Symbol of note embodied by cat

indicators.note: being embodied by means held inside the body of the other piece

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A symbol of musical note embodied in a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or object serving as the revered symbol of a clan.

clue.text: New path surprisingly leads to heavy artillery compound

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: HA is a military abbreviation for heavy artillery

explanation.surface: A new route unexpectedly brings big guns to the chemical works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges PATH as APHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a volatile hydrocarbon mixture, a chemical substance distilled from petroleum or coal tar.

clue.text: Style hint

definitions.meaning: good ... is stylish judgement in dress or design
a small hint or suggestion of something

explanation.definitionFit: Taste means aesthetic discernment, i.e. style; a taste of something is a trace or hint of it.

clue.text: Faith originally held by communist

parts.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a kind of communist

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of 'held' is taken

explanation.surface: A belief first held by a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Troth is an old word for loyalty or a pledged word, as in 'plight one's troth'.

clue.text: Break team's opponents in game

parts.note: a team of eleven players, as in cricket or football, plus the 's
in bridge, East and South sit as opponents

explanation.surface: A pause while the team's rivals are mid-match.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, partners sit North-South and East-West, so E and S are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack or tea break taken around eleven o'clock.

clue.text: Matter in the main well liquefied?

definitions.text: Matter in the main well liquefied?

indicators.note: something liquefied loses its form, so the letters are melted down and recast
in the main means mostly, so most of the word, all but a last letter, is used

explanation.surface: Is this matter that has melted, mostly?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' trims WELL to WEL; 'liquefied' rearranges MATTER + WEL. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Meltwater is water from melted snow or ice: frozen matter that has turned liquid.

clue.text: Change of heart makes little sense

indicators.note: the heart is the middle letter, which is swapped for another

parts.note: small means little

explanation.surface: A change of heart makes little sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart' swaps SMALL's central A for E.
explanation.definitionFit: Smell is one of the five senses, so it is an example of a sense.
